title: Live feed
summary: Polls stats.example.com every 1h, one request each time, for Monthly recurring revenue, Active users.
changes: The add-on is now live-feed, the one every feed is filled from. A number can be money, written as an amount and its currency. A number can be dated from the answer, a day or an instant, rather than when the answer arrived. A feed asked in whole days can say the time of day and the zone. An id too long for its poll is refused in a sentence rather than cut short, and past twenty numbers a second poll of the same address is made. Now draws its own icon.

fill.id: A name for the feed, lower case, digits and hyphens. The pack is feed-<id> and its poll feed_<id>, which is 32 characters at most, so an id longer than 27 is refused, or longer than 25 past twenty numbers.
fill.url: The whole https:// address that answers the numbers as JSON, written out and never computed. Its host is what the owner approves.
fill.every: How often it is asked. 1h for numbers that move within a day, 1d for numbers that do not.
fill.at: The time of day it is asked, such as 07:00, for a feed asked every 1d, 2d or 1w. Optional.
fill.tz: The time zone that time is read in, such as Africa/Cairo. Optional, and only beside a time of day.
fill.grant: The label of the key in the vault, which the request sends as a bearer token. A label and never the key itself. Leave it out for an address that answers anybody.
fill.project: The project the numbers are about, as its id or spoken id (things#1), so each reading lands on it. Optional.
fill.organisation: The organisation the numbers are about, as its id or spoken id (organisations#1). Optional, and only for a readings list that has an organisation field.
fill.measures: Each number and where it is in the answer: a name as the Dashboard shows it, a path (data.mrr), a unit (USD, users) and int when a fraction is wrong. Money says its currency, and minor when the answer counts cents, and is written as an amount. A number dated in the answer names the path to its date, read as a day or an instant; left out, it is dated when the answer arrived. No name twice. Twenty numbers are one request; past twenty a second poll asks the same address again.

author: BrainDog
